title: Glossary > Capacitive pressure sensor
text: A capacitive pressure sensor has two electrodes separated by a soft dielectric layer. Pressing it makes the dielectric thinner, so capacitance rises. The size of the change depends on how soft the dielectric is and on its relative permittivity.

title: Glossary > Capacitance
text: For a parallel-plate sensor, C = ε0 · εr · A / d, where ε0 is the vacuum permittivity, εr the relative permittivity of the dielectric, A the electrode area and d the dielectric thickness. Capacitance is larger for a higher permittivity, a larger area and a thinner layer.

title: Glossary > Relative permittivity (dielectric constant, εr)
text: How strongly a material polarizes in an electric field compared with vacuum, as a plain number. Vacuum and air are about 1, silicone rubber is about 2.6 to 3, and barium titanate ceramic can exceed 1000. It depends on frequency, temperature and the exact phase or grade.

title: Glossary > ΔC/C0
text: The relative capacitance change: (C - C0) / C0, where C0 is the capacitance with no pressure applied. It is the sensor's normalized response.

title: Glossary > Sensitivity
text: The slope of the response with pressure, usually in kPa^-1. In Sensora the interval-average sensitivity over a pressure range is (response at Pmax - response at Pmin) / (Pmax - Pmin).

title: Glossary > Nonlinearity
text: How far the response curve departs from a straight line over the range. Sensora's device ranking measures the largest deviation from the endpoint chord as a percentage of the full-scale response.

title: Glossary > Matrix
text: The continuous soft polymer that forms the body of the dielectric, such as Sylgard 184 (PDMS), Ecoflex, TPU, SEBS, VHB, LDPE, PVDF, P(VDF-TrFE), Kapton or PET. It mostly sets how soft the sensor is.

title: Glossary > Filler
text: Particles dispersed in the matrix, here dielectric ceramics such as TiO2, ZnO, BaTiO3, SrTiO3, Al2O3, SiO2, ZrO2, MgO, h-BN and AlN. High-permittivity fillers raise the composite's permittivity but also stiffen it slightly.

title: Glossary > Volume fraction (vol%) and weight fraction (wt%)
text: vol% is the share of the composite's volume taken by the filler, which is what the mixing laws use. wt% is the share of its mass. Heavy ceramics have a much smaller vol% than wt%, so the two must not be confused.

title: Glossary > Percolation
text: When conductive filler particles touch and form a continuous path, the composite changes abruptly from insulating to conducting. Sensora's model covers only insulating or semiconducting dielectric fillers and has no percolation model.

title: Glossary > Young's modulus
text: The stiffness of a material under small compression, in pascals. A lower modulus means the layer compresses more at a given pressure.

title: Glossary > Poisson ratio
text: The ratio of sideways expansion to compression. Near 0.5 means the material is almost incompressible, like rubber. It enters the response because the electrode area grows as the layer is squeezed.

title: Glossary > Strain and the 10% limit
text: Engineering strain is pressure divided by modulus. Sensora's small-strain model is only used up to 10% strain; candidates whose worst-case strain at the maximum pressure exceeds 10% are excluded.

title: Glossary > Maxwell-Garnett mixing rule
text: A formula for the effective permittivity of a composite with a small amount of separated spherical particles in a continuous matrix. It assumes good dispersion and no clusters.

title: Glossary > Mori-Tanaka elasticity
text: A method for estimating the effective stiffness (Young's modulus and Poisson ratio) of a matrix containing a small fraction of separated inclusions.

title: Glossary > Robust score
text: The optimizer's ranking number: a conservative relative permittivity multiplied by a conservative interval-average ΔC/C0 sensitivity. For a fixed electrode area and thickness it is proportional to the absolute capacitance sensitivity.

title: Glossary > Strain margin
text: The 10% strain limit minus the worst-case strain at the maximum requested pressure, in percentage points. A larger margin means the design is further from the limit of the model.

title: Glossary > Genetic algorithm (GA)
text: A search method that evolves a population of candidate formulations over many iterations using selection, crossover and mutation. Sensora's population size and iteration count control how thorough the search is; a fixed random seed makes runs reproducible.

title: Glossary > Hysteresis
text: The difference between the sensor's response when pressure is increasing and decreasing. Viscoelastic polymers such as VHB show strong hysteresis. Sensora's model does not include it.

title: Glossary > Dielectric loss
text: Energy lost as heat when the dielectric is cycled in an electric field, often described by the loss tangent. Conductive or semiconducting fillers can raise it. Sensora's model does not include it.

title: Glossary > Quarantined record
text: A reviewed literature device whose measured curve has a documented problem, such as a duplicated file or a nonzero response at zero pressure. Quarantined curves are kept for auditing but never ranked.

title: Glossary > Provisional and screening-ready
text: Evidence labels on material records. Screening-ready values come from a well-matched source; provisional values need a grade, direction, rate or test-mode caveat. The optimizer's stress test applies a wider margin to provisional values.

title: Composite model > Purpose and boundary
text:
This track explores nonporous planar dielectric layers made from a continuous polymer matrix and less than 5 vol% total dielectric filler. The current library has ten matrices and ten fillers. The live optimizer uses 0.1 vol% genes and permits one to four active fillers. A separate integer-loading catalogue contains 10,000 formulations for database inspection and exact benchmark tests.

This is a forward physics screen. It does not learn a mapping from the ten complete devices in the empirical database, because those devices do not isolate constituent properties under matched fabrication and measurement conditions.

title: Composite model > Constituent properties
Composite model > Constituent properties
text: The filler set is restricted to materials that can at least be represented by the present dilute dielectric mixing law. Conductive and percolating fillers require complex, frequency-dependent electrical properties and a percolation or impedance model, so they are outside this implementation.

title: Composite model > Mixing laws
text:
For spherical dilute inclusions, the multi-inclusion Maxwell-Garnett estimate is

$$\epsilon_c=\epsilon_m\frac{1+2\sum_i\phi_i\beta_i}{1-\sum_i\phi_i\beta_i},\qquad
\beta_i=\frac{\epsilon_i-\epsilon_m}{\epsilon_i+2\epsilon_m}.$$

Effective bulk and shear moduli are computed with generalized Mori-Tanaka concentration factors. They are then converted to effective Young's modulus and Poisson ratio. The implementation is in `sensora.composite_physics`.

The assumptions behind both laws are stronger than “loading below 5%.” They require separated inclusions, a continuous isotropic matrix, representative constituent properties, good bonding, and negligible aggregation and voids. Low loading only makes those assumptions more plausible.

title: Composite model > Pressure response
text:
For engineering compression strain $e=P/E_c$, constant permittivity, and freely expanding lateral dimensions, the baseline model is

$$\frac{\Delta C}{C_0}=\frac{(1+\nu_c e)^2}{1-e}-1.$$

For laterally fixed electrodes, the numerator is one. The code rejects any pressure that produces more than 10% nominal strain. A hyperelastic law and measured compression curve are required beyond that region.

Relative permittivity cancels from this normalized response when it is pressure-independent. It still controls baseline capacitance

$$C_0=\epsilon_0\epsilon_c A_0/d_0,$$

but absolute capacitance additionally requires electrode area and dielectric thickness. The present user input does not include geometry, so the model reports relative permittivity enhancement rather than inventing $C_0$.

title: Composite model > Optimization objective
text:
For fixed electrode area and starting thickness, absolute capacitance sensitivity is proportional to relative permittivity times normalized response sensitivity. The geometry-independent optimization objective is therefore

$$J=\epsilon_c^-\frac{r^-(P_{max})-r^-(P_{min})}{P_{max}-P_{min}},$$

where the minus superscript denotes a conservative property scenario. Multiplying $J$ by $\epsilon_0A_0/d_0$ gives the corresponding absolute capacitance sensitivity for a chosen geometry. This lets the optimizer reward a high effective dielectric constant without asking the user for geometry and while still accounting for composite compliance.

title: Composite model > Optimization objective
text: Robustness is an explicit engineering stress test. For `screening_ready` inputs, Young's modulus is perturbed by ±10%, relative permittivity is reduced by 10%, and Poisson ratio is reduced by 0.02. For `provisional` inputs, the corresponding margins are ±25%, −25%, and −0.05. The objective uses increased modulus, reduced permittivity, and reduced Poisson ratio. Feasibility uses reduced modulus and requires the maximum pressure to remain at or below 10% strain. These margins are policy assumptions for conservative ranking; they are not measured uncertainty distributions or statistical confidence intervals.

title: Composite model > Genetic representation
text: Each individual contains one matrix gene and one loading gene for every allowed filler. Repair keeps at most four active fillers, rounds loading to 0.1 vol%, and caps total filler at 4.9 vol%. Tournament selection, uniform crossover, mutation, and elitism evolve a population for a number of generations. The app exposes both as inputs (population 2–200, default 20; iterations 10–300, default 50); the library defaults remain 120 and 60. Small populations seed only the first matrix/filler pairs, so results can depend on the random seed. A fixed seed makes identical requests reproducible. The algorithm reports the number of unique and feasible formulations evaluated plus the convergence history. As with any GA, it does not prove that the mathematical global optimum was found.

title: Composite model > Validation evidence
Composite model > Running the screen
text:
The Streamlit interface and optimizer calculate response after the user submits a pressure interval. The database stores material properties, not a pressure-response lookup table. Fitness uses calculated endpoint responses, and 101-point nominal curves are generated for the returned optimized formulations.

At high requested pressures, soft matrices can exceed the model's 10% strain limit and are excluded candidate by candidate. Extending those matrices beyond this boundary requires a calibrated finite-strain hyperelastic law and matched capacitance measurements; increasing the number of calculated pressure points cannot supply that missing physics.

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/optimize_composites.py --pmin-kpa 0 --pmax-kpa 10
```

This writes optimized formulations, response curves, convergence history, and the complete optimization report to `artifacts/recommendations/composite_optimization`. The exact integer benchmark remains available through `scripts/screen_composites.py`. Neither search method can repair a missing pressure-dependent physical mechanism.

title: Composite model > Experimental data required before predictive optimization
text: Use a single fixed device geometry and fabrication protocol. Measure at least three batches and repeated specimens for the unfilled control plus 1, 2, 3, and 4 vol% fillers. Record actual loading, density, dispersion images, void fraction, dielectric spectrum and loss, conductivity, small-strain compression loading/unloading, thickness, area, baseline capacitance, and full pressure response with uncertainty. Those matched data can calibrate pressure-dependent permittivity or a correction term while keeping an uncalibrated formulation group for external validation.

title: Workflow > Composite-design user process
text:
1. Open **Composite optimizer**.
2. Choose the database matrices and fillers that may be considered.
3. Enter the minimum and maximum pressure in kPa.
4. Select **Find best formulations**.
5. Review the optimized formulations, predicted response curves, constituent properties, evidence status, and GA convergence.

There are no user controls for cost, target sensitivity, training, geometry, or filler loading. The only algorithm controls are the GA population size (2–200, default 20) and iteration count (10–300, default 50); all other GA settings are fixed. The seeded GA chooses a matrix, one to four fillers, and 0.1 vol% loading increments below 5 vol% total. It ranks candidates by conservative geometry-normalized capacitance sensitivity and rejects candidates whose worst-case strain exceeds 10%.

title: Workflow > Complete-device evidence behavior
text:
The program evaluates every allowed record. A device is eligible only when usable evidence covers the complete requested range. It never extrapolates beyond reported intervals or digitized curve endpoints. Quarantined curves cannot be ranked.

For records with source-reported interval sensitivities, the program constructs a continuous piecewise-linear response by integrating those interval slopes. For the other usable records, it interpolates only within the reviewed digitized observations. It computes interval-average sensitivity from the two requested endpoints and full-scale nonlinearity from deviation from the endpoint chord.

Results are ordered by higher interval-average sensitivity and then lower nonlinearity. This is an exact comparison of the allowed finite database. The output claim is limited to “best measured option within the allowed reviewed database for the requested range.”

title: Workflow > Application components
text:
| Component | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app.py` | Streamlit entry point |
| `literature_db.py` | Read and install reviewed SQLite data |
| `empirical_selection.py` | Coverage checks, interpolation, metrics, exact ranking |
| `composite_optimization.py` | Robust objective, constraints, seeded GA, convergence, and optimized curves |
| `composite_screening.py` | Exact discrete benchmark used for model checks |
| `optimizer_ui.py` | Pressure-range and allowed-option interface |
| `scripts/install_reviewed_database.py` | Rebuild SQLite from reviewed exports |
| `scripts/generate_recommendations.py` | Command-line selection and exports |

The internal database page exposes devices, curve audits, properties, sources, unresolved issues, corrections, constituent candidates, property evidence, composite formulations, and pressure-validation evidence. Downloads include ranked options, the selected response, a reproducibility report, and a database snapshot.

title: Workflow > Composite command-line workflow
text:
The same robust optimizer exposed by the primary interface has a reproducible command-line workflow. It estimates dielectric and elastic properties, evolves matrix/filler/loading genes, applies conservative material-property perturbations, and generates response curves for the returned optima. Run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/optimize_composites.py --pmin-kpa 0 --pmax-kpa 10
```

Outputs go to `artifacts/recommendations/composite_optimization` and include optimized formulations, predicted curves, GA convergence, and a reproducibility report. Material evidence status is retained in every result, and every pressure curve is labeled as a model prediction. See `docs/homogeneous_composite_model.md` for assumptions, equations, robustness policy, and required validation.

title: Workflow > Maintenance
text:
The canonical sources for a reinstall are `data/review` and `data/material_properties`. Run:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/install_reviewed_database.py
```

This transactionally replaces the application tables. Do not add a record to the usable set until its device identity, pressure-response trace, response normalization, pressure range, and source are verified. Keep questionable data in the database with a quarantine status and a concrete reason.

The removed raw directory is not required at runtime. The reviewed workbook retains the original worksheet, while reviewed and quarantined curve exports retain every original point with its source filename and row number.

title: Workflow > Managing materials
text: The **Database** page lists the available matrices and fillers. Use *Add Matrix* or *Add Filler* to insert a record (the ID is assigned automatically), or select rows and press *Delete Selected*. Records cannot be edited in place. New materials need a name, Young's modulus, Poisson ratio, relative permittivity, and density; they are treated as provisional by the robustness stress test. Every change is backed up first under `data/catalog/backups`.

title: Device selection method > Scope
text:
Sensora ranks reviewed, already-characterized capacitive pressure sensors for a requested pressure interval. The input is the pressure range plus the set of permitted database records. The output is a ranking of records with complete usable coverage.

This is an empirical selection problem. The current evidence does not identify independent matrix modulus, filler permittivity, volume fraction, geometry response, and interaction parameters for arbitrary recombination. Consequently, the software does not claim to predict new mixtures from these ten devices.

title: Device selection method > Response construction
text:
For D001–D003 and D010, the source reports sensitivities on contiguous pressure intervals. If interval j has sensitivity S_j over [a_j,b_j], the relative response is constructed as

$$r(P)=\sum_j S_j\max(0,\min(P,b_j)-a_j).$$

This uses the published slopes and fixes r(0)=0. It is piecewise linear and is used only within the union of the reported contiguous intervals.

For D004, D005, and D009, the system uses the reviewed digitized pressure-response observations. Linear interpolation is permitted between adjacent observations; extrapolation outside their endpoints is prohibited.

D006 is a duplicated D008 file with an incorrect device ID. D007 and D008 report nonzero `(C-C0)/C0` at zero pressure. These three traces are quarantined and never ranked.

title: Device selection method > Metrics and ranking
text:
For a requested interval [P_min,P_max], the average sensitivity is

$$S_{avg}=\frac{r(P_{max})-r(P_{min})}{P_{max}-P_{min}}.$$

Nonlinearity is the maximum absolute deviation from the endpoint chord divided by the interval's full-scale response, expressed as a percentage. A zero or negative response span is rejected.

Eligible records are sorted by decreasing average sensitivity and then increasing nonlinearity. Device ID gives deterministic ordering after exact ties. Cost is not calculated.

title: Device selection method > Why complete-device selection does not use a genetic algorithm
text:
There are ten independent complete-device records, so every allowed option can be evaluated directly. A genetic algorithm would sample a space that can be exhaustively checked in milliseconds and could miss the best record. It also cannot make scientifically valid new combinations without a forward model whose required constituent and architecture parameters are missing. Exact enumeration therefore gives a reproducible global ranking within the allowed database.

This restriction applies only to the retained complete-device evidence utilities and not to the application workflow. The primary **Composite optimizer** has an explicit constituent-property forward model and uses a seeded GA to optimize matrix, filler identities, and volume fractions. Its robust objective and constraints are documented in `docs/homogeneous_composite_model.md`.

title: Device selection method > Evidence limits
text:
The ranking compares heterogeneous literature measurements. Frequency, temperature, fabrication variation, test fixture, cycling, hysteresis, uncertainty, and curve digitization are not consistently matched. Published interval sensitivities may not agree exactly with digitized plots because of source definitions and plotting resolution. The output is a screening result for the available evidence, not proof that one sensor will outperform another in a new experiment.

Before treating any option as validated, reproduce its fabrication, measure loading and unloading replicates under matched conditions, record baseline capacitance and uncertainty, and compare the full measured curve with the stored response.

title: Literature notes
text: These notes come from a limited web search and from this project's reviewed device records. They are not a systematic review.

title: Literature notes > Multiple fillers in one composite
text: Reports of two fillers in one dielectric exist. Within the reviewed devices, D005 uses BaTiO3 with multi-walled carbon nanotubes (Materials Letters 2021, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.matlet.2021.130512) and D006 to D008 use carbon black with carbon nanotubes (Micromachines 2022, https://www.mdpi.com/2072-666x/13/2/223). A PDMS, BaTiO3 and SrTiO3 dielectric has also been reported (https://scielo.br/j/rmat/a/fMggn75jYP46QLLZrLCtHwz), as has BaTiO3 combined with ketjenblack in silicone rubber (https://idr.nitk.ac.in/handle/123456789/24477). The project's validation set PR-V003 uses PDMS with TiO2 and ZnO. No study with three or more filler types in one dielectric was found. Mixed fillers are usually a ceramic plus a conductive filler, or two ceramics.

title: Literature notes > More than one matrix
text: All ten reviewed devices use PDMS alone. A polymer blend of PDMS with polyurethane has been reported to raise permittivity in an actuator study (https://joam.inoe.ro/articles/a-study-on-a-polyurethane-based-blend-with-enhanced-electromechanical-properties/fulltext), but no capacitive pressure sensor with a measured matrix blend was found. Layered dielectrics, such as a PVDF fibre layer on a PDMS array (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/pmid/38894295), are multilayer devices and not a single blended matrix. Sensora's multi-matrix option is a miscible-blend assumption with logarithmic mixing and Voigt and Reuss modulus bounds; it has not been validated against measured blends.

title: Literature notes > Why interfaces and structure matter
text: A study of EPDM composites found that filler-matrix interfaces can outweigh a filler's own permittivity, and that carbon black interacting with ceramics casts doubt on standard mixing rules (https://zeus.plmsc.psu.edu/~manias/PDFs/MRS-Adv_elastomer-CB_2021.pdf). Micro-structured and porous dielectrics often give much higher sensitivity than solid layers, and porosity and microstructure are not in Sensora's model.

title: Literature notes > Model-form gap
text: The static mixing laws cannot reproduce the very large low-pressure sensitivity reported for the PDMS, TiO2 and ZnO composite in PR-V003 (2.79 per kPa over 0 to 1.5 kPa). Predictions for filled composites should be treated as hypotheses until measured.

title: Reviewed sensor literature data
text:
Start with **capacitive_pressure_sensor_10v1_reviewed.xlsx**, opening `Reviewed_devices`.
This is the corrected reference dataset used to build the internal SQLite database. It supports selection among complete reported devices; it is **not a constituent-property catalogue for generating new combinations**. The original worksheet is retained as `Original_devices` inside the reviewed workbook. Every former raw curve point is retained, with its source filename and row, in either `review_only_curves.csv` or `quarantined_curves.csv`.

title: Reviewed data > Workbook and CSV contents
text:
- `Original_devices`: original worksheet values for comparison.
- `Reviewed_devices`: ten device records with corrected labels, review status and explicit optimizer blockers. Unchanged fields retain their supplied meaning and are not automatically verified.
- `Changes`: ten cell corrections, previous/new values, source and location.
- `Properties`: source-specific measurements and reported sensitivities. These are separate from intrinsic matrix properties. Pressure intervals apply to individual reported sensitivity values, not to a validated model domain.
- `Curve_audit`: identity, duplication, numerical, baseline and range checks for every supplied CSV. Observed pressure endpoints are not validated operating limits.
- `Unresolved`: missing evidence and the action required before use.
- `Sources`: primary references and the extent of verification. P01/P04 XML snapshots are in `sources`; other checks used publisher-indexed text or the author-shared paper. P05 full text could not be verified.

title: Reviewed data > Workbook and CSV contents
text: Each review sheet also has a CSV companion. `review_only_curves.csv` contains 130 unchanged points from seven files. **Review-only does not mean validated:** trace identity, digitization calibration, measurement conditions and uncertainty still need verification. `quarantined_curves.csv` retains all 57 points from the three problematic files with their original IDs, filenames and row numbers. Neither export is loaded by the active application.

title: Reviewed data > Corrections and evidence
text:
D005 includes both BaTiO3 and MWCNT: its CNT flag, filler count and class are corrected from the [P03 abstract](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167577X2101209X). Its loading denominator and CNT quantity remain unknown.

D006–D008 are planar PCDL variants in [P04, Figure 7c](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8880179/). D007's 2.5 MPa value belongs to the filled composite, so it is removed from the matrix field and retained with its scope. Composite permittivities are recorded separately at 1 MHz.

D004's loading basis is corrected to grams of BT per 100 g PDMS/water emulsion: the [P02 methods](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ceramint.2022.01.191) add 2 g BT to 10 g emulsion. This is not final dry-composite wt% or vol%. Water removal and retained solids must be accounted for before conversion.

title: Reviewed data > Corrections and evidence
text:
D010's modulus and permittivity describe porous material, not bulk PDMS. They are relocated using [P06, Table 2 and tensile methods](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/acssensors.0c02122). PS1/D1 is matched by the supplied 110 C cure and properties; exact curve identity remains to be checked. The table's sensitivities are converted from percent/kPa to kPa^-1 by dividing by 100. No such conversion is applied to the supplied CSV, whose header already declares a dimensionless response.

[P01, Table 2](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10422564/) supplies interval sensitivities for D001–D003; these are published measurements, not fits to the supplied CSVs. Their nominal 20:1 and 10:1 matrix/filler ratios support the supplied rounded 4.76 and 9.09 wt% values, but not a volume-fraction conversion.

title: Reviewed data > Curve problems requiring original measurements or re-digitization
text:
| Device | Finding | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| D001–D003 | No zero-pressure point; some points extend beyond the 50 kPa table interval | Retain with warnings; verify axes, calibration and trace |
| D006 | File contains D008 IDs and is byte-identical to D008 | Quarantine duplicate; D006's correct curve is still missing |
| D007 | At zero pressure, normalized response is 0.73 | Quarantine pending normalization/axis review |
| D008 | At zero pressure, normalized response is 0.58 | Quarantine pending normalization/axis review |
| D009 | Digitizer notes assume loading branch; publisher full text unavailable | Retain as unverified; preserve original metadata |

For `(C-C0)/C0`, the zero-pressure response should be zero when C0 is the same zero-pressure baseline. A mismatch can indicate an incorrect axis, baseline, trace or digitization. Subtracting an offset without that evidence is not a justified correction. No artificial baseline or missing curve has been inserted.

title: Reviewed data > What is still needed
text:
All ten records have the historical `optimizer_ready=False` flag because they cannot drive the former constituent-mixing model. A measured device curve alone does not identify independent constituent properties. Generic PDMS constants, composite values and tensile moduli must not be substituted silently.

The live application now uses these records through `data/catalog/sensor_data.sqlite3`. Seven devices can be ranked as complete-device measurements within supported ranges; three remain quarantined. The two user inputs remain pressure range and allowed database options.

title: Reviewed data > Reproduce
text:
From the project root:

```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/install_reviewed_database.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q
```

`manifest.json` retains the checksums recorded during the original review. The standalone raw files were intentionally removed after integration; the reviewed workbook and curve exports are now the canonical traceable source for database installation.

title: Dilute homogeneous-composite evidence
text: This directory is the traceable starting dataset for a physics-based compositional search. It is separate from the complete-device literature records in `data/review` because constituent properties and sensor response curves have different scientific meanings.

title: Material properties data > Search domain
text:
The domain contains ten polymer matrices and ten dielectric filler candidates. `search_space.csv` is a discrete benchmark containing all 10,000 integer matrix/allocation pairs at 1-4 total vol%, including formulations with one to four active filler types. The live GA uses the same materials at 0.1 vol% resolution, with total filler capped at 4.9 vol%.

The matrices are Sylgard 184, Ecoflex 00-30, TPU, SEBS H1053, VHB 4910, LDPE, PVDF, P(VDF-TrFE), Kapton HN, and PET. The fillers are TiO2, ZnO, BaTiO3, SrTiO3, Al2O3, SiO2, ZrO2, MgO, h-BN, and AlN. Conductive fillers such as CNT, graphene, carbon black, MXene, and metals are excluded from this model because Maxwell-Garnett with real-valued permittivity does not describe their frequency-dependent conductivity or percolation behavior.

title: Material properties data > Search domain
Material properties data > Files
text:
- `model_materials.csv`: one selected nominal property set per candidate material.
- `property_evidence.csv`: every selected or comparison property with conditions and provenance.
- `sources.csv`: source registry.
- `search_space.csv`: all integer filler allocations with total filler below 5 vol% for every matrix.
- `scripts/build_material_search_space.py`: deterministic generator for `search_space.csv`.
- `pressure_response_validation.csv`: one digitized flat-PDMS curve and two curves reconstructed from explicitly reported linear sensitivities.
- `dielectric_validation.csv`: reported and fit-reconstructed PDMS/TiO2 permittivity evidence.

`reported_fit_reconstruction` rows are not raw observations. They implement the published slope over the stated interval and enforce zero normalized response at zero pressure. `figure_digitized` rows are approximate readings from a published plot and include a conservative response uncertainty. Neither type should be relabeled as directly supplied tabular measurements.

title: Material properties data > Important scientific result
text:
For a parallel-plate capacitor,

$$\frac{\Delta C}{C_0}=\frac{\epsilon(P)}{\epsilon(0)}\frac{A(P)}{A_0}\frac{d_0}{d(P)}-1.$$

If permittivity is constant, filler permittivity cancels from the normalized response. It raises baseline capacitance but does not directly raise `delta_C/C0`. In that baseline model, the response is controlled by thickness compression, lateral area change, and the effective elastic constants. A filler can even reduce normalized sensitivity by stiffening the composite.

The 2026 homogeneous PDMS/TiO2/ZnO paper reports a much larger sensitivity after adding only 0.5 wt% of each filler. That result indicates effects absent from the baseline model, such as pressure-dependent polarization, interfaces, altered mechanics, or device/test details. It is valuable validation evidence, but it prevents a scientifically honest claim that Maxwell-Garnett plus linear compression alone predicts the measured composite response.

title: Material properties data > Important scientific result
text: The PDMS/TiO2 dielectric study presents a second warning. Its reported low-loading fit rises from 3.02 by about 0.77 per vol% TiO2, whereas Maxwell-Garnett with constituent values 3.02 and 80 predicts only about 3.36 at 4 vol%. The model should therefore report this discrepancy instead of treating the mixing law as experimentally validated.

title: Material properties data > What must be measured next
text: Fabricate at least the unfilled control and 1-4 vol% formulations under one fixed protocol. For each batch, measure density or actual volume fraction, microscopy-based dispersion, dielectric spectrum, loss/conductivity, small-strain compression with loading and unloading, initial thickness and electrode area, baseline capacitance, and replicate `delta_C/C0` versus pressure. These matched measurements are needed before a GA fitness score can be called predictive.

title: Device D001
text: Reviewed literature device D001 (paper P01): matrix PDMS; filler none; loading 0 wt%; structure Microstructured; electrodes Copper foil + polyimide tape. Curve status: usable for ranking. Reported properties: reported interval sensitivity 1.3 kPa^-1 over 0 to 2 kPa (complete sensor); reported interval sensitivity 0.17 kPa^-1 over 2 to 15 kPa (complete sensor); reported interval sensitivity 0.04 kPa^-1 over 15 to 50 kPa (complete sensor).

title: Device D002
text: Reviewed literature device D002 (paper P01): matrix PDMS; filler BaTiO3; loading 4.76 wt% (nominal, PDMS:BaTiO3 = 20:1); structure Microstructured; electrodes Copper foil + polyimide tape. Curve status: usable for ranking.
